question: What is Index-Free Adjacency in graph databases?
category: What is Index-Free Adjacency in graph databases?

options.text: Each node maintains direct memory/disk pointers to its adjacent neighbor relationships, enabling $O(1)$ step traversals independent of total graph size.
Relational databases must compute expensive join tables on primary/foreign keys ($O(N \log N)$), while graphs traverse pre-linked pointers ($O(K)$).
It uses Breadth-First Search (BFS) to find the minimum-hop relationship path between two nodes.
